questions.stem: A client with a markedly weakened immune system asks how to reduce foodborne-infection risk at home. Which instruction is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use refrigerated deli meats without reheating because refrigeration alone is considered sufficient to control foodborne risk in a weakened immune system.","B":"Choose pasteurized dairy and washed produce, but include undercooked eggs when the shells are intact and the eggs have remained refrigerated.","C":"Choose fully cooked meat and eggs, but include raw sprouts after thorough rinsing because washing is considered adequate for this higher-risk food.","D":"Choose fully cooked meat and eggs, pasteurized dairy, and washed produce, and heat deli meats until steaming hot or 165°F before serving them."}}
questions.rationale: People with weakened immune systems have greater risk from foodborne illness. Option D is correct because CDC identifies thoroughly cooked meat and eggs, pasteurized dairy, washed produce, and reheated deli meats as safer choices. Option A is incorrect because unheated deli meats are a higher-risk choice. Option B is incorrect because undercooked eggs remain higher risk. Option C is incorrect because raw sprouts remain a higher-risk choice even after rinsing.
questions.source_name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — Safer Food Choices for People With Weakened Immune Systems
questions.source_detail: CDC guidance current on its food-safety site and rechecked August 14, 2026 identifies undercooked meat and eggs, unpasteurized dairy, unwashed produce, raw sprouts, and unheated deli meats as higher-risk choices for people with weakened immune systems.

questions.stem: A nurse is communicating with an alert client who has significant hearing impairment. Which approach is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Face the client in good lighting, speak clearly at a normal volume and pace, and use written or other preferred communication methods when helpful.","B":"Face the client but substantially increase volume and exaggerate mouth movements because louder, exaggerated speech improves understanding with hearing loss.","C":"Speak from the client's better-hearing side while looking toward the chart because visual access to the speaker's face adds little when hearing is impaired.","D":"Direct most questions to a companion and let the companion relay answers because hearing loss makes direct client communication less reliable."}}
questions.rationale: Communication should be adapted to the client's hearing needs. Option A is correct because facing the client in good lighting, speaking clearly without shouting, and using preferred written or other methods can improve communication. Option B is incorrect because shouting and exaggerated speech can distort communication. Option C removes visual access to the speaker's face. Option D unnecessarily redirects communication away from the competent client.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf / Open RN — Nursing Fundamentals: Communication
questions.source_detail: Open RN Nursing Fundamentals, 2nd edition (2024), provides communication strategies for hearing impairment including facing the client in a well-lit environment, facilitating visual access, speaking clearly without shouting, and using the client's preferred communication methods.

questions.stem: A nurse is caring for an alert client with significant visual impairment. Which communication approach is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Identify yourself after beginning care, then move personal items as needed without describing the changes because touch will help the client locate them later.","B":"Use touch to announce your presence and rely mainly on gestures during care because verbal descriptions provide little benefit when vision is impaired.","C":"Speak primarily to a companion about the environment and procedures because the companion can later explain visual details to the client afterward.","D":"Identify yourself when entering, provide adequate lighting, read pertinent information aloud, and describe locations of important items verbally as needed."}}
questions.rationale: Communication with visual impairment should maximize verbal orientation and accessible information. Option D is correct because the nurse identifies self, provides appropriate lighting, reads pertinent information aloud, and verbally describes item locations. Option A moves belongings without orientation. Option B relies on gestures that the client may not see. Option C unnecessarily redirects communication to a companion rather than the client.
questions.source_name: NCBI Bookshelf / Open RN — Nursing Fundamentals: Communication
questions.source_detail: Open RN Nursing Fundamentals, 2nd edition (2024), provides strategies for visual impairment including identifying oneself, using adequate lighting, reading pertinent information aloud, and verbally describing locations of important items.

questions.stem: After an uncomplicated diagnostic lumbar puncture, a client asks whether remaining flat for several hours is necessary solely to prevent a post-dural-puncture headache. Which response is most accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Remain flat for several hours after the procedure because prolonged bed rest has been shown to prevent post-dural-puncture headache after lumbar puncture.","B":"Drink extra fluids specifically to prevent headache because aggressive hydration has been shown to stop cerebrospinal-fluid leakage after lumbar puncture.","C":"Avoid upright activity until the next day because sitting or walking after lumbar puncture is known to increase persistent cerebrospinal-fluid leakage.","D":"Prolonged bed rest is not shown to prevent post-puncture headache; follow postprocedure instructions and mobilize as clinically appropriate when allowed."}}
questions.rationale: Current evidence does not support routine prolonged bed rest after lumbar puncture solely to prevent post-dural-puncture headache; Cochrane found that bed rest does not prevent the headache and may increase it, and extra fluids have not shown preventive benefit. Option D is correct. Option A incorrectly claims prolonged flat positioning is preventive. Option B overstates hydration as a preventive intervention. Option C incorrectly treats upright activity as a proven cause of persistent CSF leakage. Specific postprocedure instructions should still be followed for other clinical reasons.
questions.source_name: Cochrane — Body position and intake of fluids for preventing headache after a lumbar puncture
questions.source_detail: Cochrane evidence rechecked August 14, 2026 concludes routine bed rest after lumbar puncture does not prevent post-dural-puncture headache and may increase it; extra fluid intake has not shown preventive benefit.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old client asks which routine vaccinations still matter in older adulthood. Which response best reflects current CDC guidance?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Review pneumococcal vaccination by age and history, but defer recombinant zoster vaccination because increasing age makes zoster vaccination inappropriate.","B":"Recommend recombinant zoster vaccine, but omit pneumococcal vaccination unless the client has previously been hospitalized for bacterial pneumonia.","C":"Continue influenza vaccination, but discontinue age-based zoster and pneumococcal vaccination because those vaccines are intended for younger adults.","D":"Review vaccine history and give indicated recombinant zoster and pneumococcal vaccines, plus other vaccines recommended by age, history, and risk level."}}
questions.rationale: CDC adult immunization guidance continues vaccination in older adulthood based on age, history, risk factors, and prior doses. Option D is correct because recombinant zoster and pneumococcal vaccination are routinely considered in this age group along with other indicated vaccines. Option A incorrectly defers zoster vaccination because of age. Option B makes pneumococcal vaccination depend on prior hospitalization. Option C incorrectly stops age-based zoster and pneumococcal vaccination.
questions.source_name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — Adult Immunization Schedule by Age
questions.source_detail: CDC adult immunization schedule with the July 2, 2025 addendum, rechecked August 14, 2026, includes age- and risk-based recombinant zoster and pneumococcal vaccination along with other indicated adult vaccines.
